we propose a new generative model for learning the conditional joint image composition of objects from their marginal distributions and evaluate it in both paired and unpaired settings.
we propose a new framework for learning object composition in a self-consistent manner, which is conditioned on the marginal distributions of individual objects to sample from the joint distribution.
our model is able to learn the composition of two object domains given their marginal distributions, and it generalizes to unseen combinations at test time.

learning the joint distributions of the individual object domains, which is the first step towards learning the joint distribution over the scene domain.
the question: How can we learn the joint distribution of two object domains and use it to compose new instances of the joint domain at test time?
the following question: how can we model the complex interactions between different entities in the world to generate realistic images of their joint distribution?

our model is able to learn to compose images of two object classes given only the marginal distributions of each object class.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we learn to generate new images from the joint distribution of the objects in a scene by modeling the conditional distribution of the objects given the scene, which is the reverse of the typical generative model.

our proposed model can be used to generate a realistic scene image from a given image of two different objects, where the objects can be of different categories and the scene is not present in the training data.

the proposed compositional generative model can be used to learn complex interactions between multiple entities in the world and generate realistic images of the joint distributions from the marginal distributions of the entities.
the composition of images can be modeled in a self-consistent manner in the context of generative models, without requiring any explicit supervision.
